correctness.rationale: The binary order-eight orientable problem is equivalent to selecting nonpalindromic 8-bit arcs in the order-seven de Bruijn graph, with at most one from each reversal pair and balanced in/out degree at every seven-bit vertex. For 16 palindromic states, reversal pairing and balance force opposite exterior bits between each selected incoming and outgoing arc. The supplied nonnegative integer dual has 120 pair classes, beta weights summing exactly 92; independent V8 arithmetic checked all 240 gamma_w>=1 (minimum 1, maximum 3) and all 44 locally admissible palindromic-state patterns. The supplied 92-bit cyclic witness has exactly 92 distinct nonpalindromic reversal classes. Thus the exact finite dual certifies upper 92 and the witness attains it; no reliance on optimization log.
